It's called an automatic transfer switch. If the grid (AKA "Shore Power") goes down and the generator kicks in (be it diesel, nattygas, solar, wind, etc) the transfer switch automatically shunts from shore to generator and (in the case of fossil fuel) starts the engine.

This transfer switch then monitors the shore power line and will switch back to it when the grid is back up and then puts the generator back into standby mode.

Source: I assisted in the installation of an 800A generator at the city hall while in the maintenance department of a small southern city and am an amateur electrician (and occasional welder)
